# Contributing

<!-- Generated by scrum-github (preset standard). Edit it freely: init never overwrites it. -->

## Branches

| Branch | What it holds | Who writes to it |
|---|---|---|
| `main` | Released code. Every version tag (`v1.2.0`) is on this branch. | Release and hotfix pull requests only |
| `develop` | Work that is done but not released yet. | Pull requests from task branches |
| `feat/<task>-<slug>`, `fix/...` | One task. Created from `develop`. | You |
| `hotfix/<task>-<slug>` | An urgent fix of a released version. Created from `main`. | You |

Code moves one way: task branch → `develop` → `main`. Only `hotfix/*` starts
from `main`. Nobody pushes to `develop` or `main` directly: every change goes
through a pull request, which needs the required checks and the review.

## Pull requests

- Target `develop`. A pull request from a task branch into `main` fails the
  source-branch check; only `release/*` and `hotfix/*` may target `main`.
- The title follows [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org): a type (`feat`,
  `fix`, `docs`, `chore`, `refactor`, `test`, `ci`, `perf`, `build`, `revert`), an optional scope,
  `!` for a breaking change, then `: ` and a summary. Example: `feat(auth): log in with email`.
- The description closes its task: `Closes #<task number>`. A change without a task gets the
  `no-task` label instead.
- Squash-merge task pull requests into `develop`. A back-merge (`main` → `develop`) is
  merged with a merge commit, never squashed.

A task merged into `develop` stays In review with the label `on: develop`; it is Done when
its code reaches `main` in a release.

## Releases

1. `/scrum-github:release` opens a release pull request from `release/<tag>` into `main`
   with the version, the release notes and the updated version files.
2. Review it and merge it with a merge commit. The release workflow then creates the tag and the
   GitHub Release, sets the released tasks Done and opens the back-merge into `develop`.
3. Merge the back-merge pull request with a merge commit.

A hotfix: `/scrum-github:hotfix <task>` creates `hotfix/<task>-<slug>` from `main`; its pull request
targets `main` and publishes a patch version when merged.
